series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$reason: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against.

country_profile.$note: Population is World Bank SP.POP.TOTL for the latest year published in the 2015-2025 window. Income group is the World Bank's own classification, not a UNFCCC one.

ndc_registry.$note: The registry states which submission is current and where it is. It carries no target figure, so nothing in ndc.* is derived from it.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "Sous l'option inconditionnelle (CPDN), les réductions d'émissions par rapport à leur trajectoire prévue sont de de 3%, 4% et 5% respectivement en 2020, 2025 et 2030. Avec l'option conditionnelle (CPDN+), les réductions d'émissions attendues sont de l'ordre de 7%, 15% et 21% sur les mêmes années." Under the unconditional scenario (INDC) emission reductions relative to baseline projections will be 3%, 4% and 5% in 2020, 2025 and 2030 respectively. Under the conditional scenario (INDC+), expected emission reductions will be 7%, 15% and 21% for the same years.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 3% (unconditional) to 7% (conditional) reduction in 2020, 4% (unconditional) to 15% (conditional) reduction in 2025, and 5% (unconditional) to 21% (conditional) reduction in 2030 in GHG emissions compared to baseline projections
ndc_assessment.sectors: Energy, Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU), Industry, Waste management
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

ndc_document.$reason: the document states targets on more than one basis or horizon (bau ·  · 2025; bau ·  · 2035); choosing between them would be a guess.

emissions_profile.$note: Headline totals are OWID only. OWID's CO₂ sub-totals are fossil/industrial CO₂ by fuel, not a full sectoral GHG breakdown, and do not sum to total_mtco2e. DS-05's rows are non-CO₂ gases only and are not comparable with the others; that is also why DS-05 is absent from series.observed, where a shorter curve would read as a disagreement rather than a difference of scope. by_source carries each source whole.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is First NDC, filed 2020-12-29. 48 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (2). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 42.9 MtCO₂e, DS-35 35.4 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. ND-GAIN scores it 42.3 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 3% (unconditional) to 7% (conditional) reduction in 2020, 4% (unconditional) to 15% (conditional) reduction in 2025, and 5% (unconditional) to 21% (conditional) reduction in 2030 in GHG emissions compared to baseline projections It was classed both. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.15°C under SSP1-2.6 to +4.41°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
